info.bio:
Two bands share the moniker: 

1.
Historically, The Winstons were a funk and soul music outfit from the 1960s who are most notable for recording a track called "Amen Brother" (a B-side to the single "Color Him Father" edited in 1969). "Amen, Brother" is probably the most sampled record of all time. Midway through the track there is a drum solo which contains the "Amen break" which has been sampled and used in thousands of hip-hop, drum and bass and jungle tracks.

xref.title: The "Amen Break" (1969)
xref.body: Gregory Coleman, the drummer for The Winstons, played the seven-second drum bit in their 1969 song "Amen Brother," which became famously known as the "Amen Break." This specific drum segment is recognized as the "most sampled piece of music in the universe," appearing in nearly 6,200 songs. "It features a seven-second drum bit by Gregory Coleman. This is the most sampled piece of music in the universe."
